name: Emergency: Call 911
summary: For any emergency where someone is hurt or in danger, call 911 right away.

name: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline
summary: Call or text 988 any time, day or night, to talk with someone who cares. It is free and private.

name: Alabama Domestic Violence Hotline
summary: If you are being hurt at home, call this free hotline any time to find safety and the nearest shelter.

name: Poison Control
summary: Call right away if someone may have swallowed or touched something harmful.

name: Cullman County Health Department
summary: The local health department offers clinic services like shots and health care by appointment on weekdays.
hours: Clinic: Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Call for an appointment.

name: Alabama Department of Rehabilitation Services
summary: Helps people with disabilities get job training and find work. The Decatur office serves Cullman County, and its toll free number is 1-800-671-6838.

name: Cullman Housing Authority
summary: Offers affordable public housing for families and individuals who qualify. Call ahead if you plan to come in during the afternoon.

name: Cullman County Extension Office (ACES)
summary: Free advice and classes on gardening, farming, food and nutrition, plus 4H for kids.

name: Alabama Career Center, Cullman
summary: Free help finding a job, building a resume and getting job training.

name: WellStone Cullman
summary: Mental health and substance use care for children, teens, adults and families, including counseling and medication management. Call the Cullman Access to Care line to get started.
hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

name: CARTS Rides
summary: Public rides anywhere in Cullman County by reservation, including shopping routes for each part of the county. Riders 60 and older and riders with disabilities pay half fare.

name: NARCOG Area Agency on Aging
summary: The regional agency on aging for Cullman County. One phone call connects you to Medicare counseling, senior meals, help at home, caregiver support and free legal help for seniors.
who: Adults 60 and older, adults of any age with disabilities, and their caregivers in Cullman, Lawrence and Morgan counties.
hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

name: Cullman County Commission on Aging
summary: The county office for senior services. It runs the full time senior centers, helps with Medicare drug plan comparisons, helps seniors apply for free medicine and sets up free legal visits.
who: Cullman County residents 60 and older. Medicine help (SenioRx) starts at age 55. During Medicare Open Enrollment (October 15 to December 7) counseling is by appointment only.
hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Closed for lunch 12:00 to 12:30.

name: Meals for Homebound Seniors
summary: Hot meals delivered to the homes of seniors who cannot easily get out, Monday to Friday except holidays. This is Cullman County's home delivered meals program, much like Meals on Wheels.
who: Homebound adults 60 and older who live in an area served by a full time senior center, including Hanceville and Colony.

name: SHIP Medicare Counseling
summary: Free, unbiased help understanding Medicare, choosing a drug plan, Medigap, Medicare Savings Programs, bills and appeals. Counselors do not sell insurance.
who: Anyone with Medicare, people about to get Medicare, and their families.

name: Alabama Department of Senior Services
summary: The state agency for older Alabamians. Call 1-800-AGE-LINE for help with senior meals, prescription help, Medicare, caregiver support and more.
who: Seniors, adults with disabilities and family caregivers anywhere in Alabama.

name: Medicaid Waiver Care at Home
summary: Medicaid waiver programs help people stay at home instead of moving to a nursing home. A case manager can set up personal care, homemaker help and other services at no cost to the family.
who: People whose doctor says they need nursing home level care and who have full Medicaid or may qualify for it. NARCOG serves Cullman, Lawrence and Morgan counties.

name: Alabama Cares Caregiver Support
summary: Help for family caregivers, including information, counseling, support groups, training and respite so you can rest.
who: Family caregivers of adults 60 and older, older relatives (not parents) raising children 18 and under, and caregivers of adults 19 to 59 with disabilities. Income does not keep you from getting help.
how: Ask for the Alabama Cares coordinator at extension 222.

name: Report Elder Abuse: Adult Abuse Hotline
summary: Call this Alabama DHR hotline if you think an older or disabled adult is being abused, neglected or taken advantage of with money.
who: Anyone can call to report. If someone is in danger right now, call 911.

name: Social Security Office, Cullman
summary: The Social Security office for Cullman County. Get help with retirement, disability, SSI, Medicare sign up and replacement cards. Calling ahead for an appointment can save you a wait.
who: Anyone with Social Security business. Many tasks can also be done online or by calling 1-800-772-1213.
hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

name: Colony Senior Center
summary: A full time Commission on Aging senior center. Seniors 60 and older can stop in for a hot lunch, activities and good company, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.
hours: Mon to Fri 8 AM to 1 PM

name: Crane Hill Senior Center
summary: A full time Commission on Aging senior center. Seniors 60 and older can stop in for a hot lunch, activities and good company, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.
hours: Mon to Fri 8 AM to 1 PM

name: Cullman Senior Center
summary: A full time Commission on Aging senior center. Seniors 60 and older can stop in for a hot lunch, activities and good company, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.
address: 1539 Sportsman Lake Road NW, Cullman, AL 35055
hours: Mon to Fri 8 AM to 1 PM

name: Fairview Senior Center
summary: A full time Commission on Aging senior center. Seniors 60 and older can stop in for a hot lunch, activities and good company, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.
hours: Mon to Fri 8 AM to 1 PM

name: Good Hope Senior Center
summary: A full time Commission on Aging senior center. Seniors 60 and older can stop in for a hot lunch, activities and good company, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.
hours: Mon to Fri 8 AM to 1 PM

name: Hanceville Senior Center
summary: A full time Commission on Aging senior center. Seniors 60 and older can stop in for a hot lunch, activities and good company, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.
hours: Mon to Fri 8 AM to 1 PM

name: Holly Pond Senior Center
summary: A full time Commission on Aging senior center. Seniors 60 and older can stop in for a hot lunch, activities and good company, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.
address: 221 Lions Park Road, Holly Pond, AL 35083
hours: Mon to Fri 8 AM to 1 PM

name: West Point Senior Center
summary: A full time Commission on Aging senior center. Seniors 60 and older can stop in for a hot lunch, activities and good company, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.
hours: Mon to Fri 8 AM to 1 PM

name: SNAP Food Assistance at Cullman County DHR
summary: Apply for SNAP (food stamps) in person, or drop off a paper application, at the Cullman County DHR office. Benefits come on an EBT card you use at the grocery store.
who: Households with low income. The amount depends on income and household size.

name: Apply for SNAP Online (MyDHR)
summary: Apply for food assistance online, check your case, renew and report changes. You will create a free account first, and your application goes to your county DHR office.
who: Alabama residents applying for or already getting SNAP.
how: Cullman County still uses MyDHR as of October 2026. A few Alabama counties have moved to DHR's new ACES Self Service Portal, and MyDHR will tell you if yours has.

name: Alabama Food Assistance Information Line
summary: The state SNAP information line for questions about food assistance.
who: Anyone with questions about SNAP in Alabama.

name: Simple SNAP Application for Seniors (AESAP)
summary: A shorter, easier SNAP application for older Alabamians.
who: Households where everyone is 65 or older and no one has earned income from a job.

name: WIC Nutrition Program
summary: WIC helps with healthy foods, nutrition advice and breastfeeding support. Apply and get benefits at the Cullman County Health Department.
who: Pregnant women, new and breastfeeding moms, babies and children under 5 who meet income guidelines.

name: Senior Farmers Market Vouchers
summary: Seniors can get $30 in vouchers to spend on fresh produce at local farmers markets in summer and fall. Supplies are limited and you must apply again each year.
who: Adults 60 and older who qualify. NARCOG helps people apply from January into spring.

name: Cullman Caring for Kids
summary: One of Cullman County's biggest food pantries. It runs the United Way Food Bank and hands out boxes of food. Monetary donations can be made at cullmancaringforkids.com.
who: Cullman County families in need. You may be asked to bring a photo ID, mail with your current address or proof of income.
hours: Monday to Thursday, 9:00 a.m. to noon and 1:00 to 3:00 p.m. Closed Friday to Sunday.
address: 402 Arnold Street NE, Suite W-1, Cullman

name: USDA National Hunger Hotline
summary: Talk with someone who can find meal sites, food banks and other food help near you. You can also text a question to 914-342-7744.
who: Anyone who needs food.
hours: Monday to Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Central time.

name: Cullman County DHR Office
summary: Your local Department of Human Resources office for food assistance, family assistance, child support, adult services and family and child services. One main number reaches every department.
who: Cullman County residents.

name: Report Child Abuse or Neglect
summary: Alabama DHR asks people to report suspected child abuse or neglect to the county DHR office or to local law enforcement. Do not report by email.
who: Anyone who is worried about a child under 19. If a child is in danger right now, call 911.

name: Adult Protective Services, Cullman County
summary: DHR looks into reports of abuse, neglect or money exploitation of elderly and disabled adults and can arrange services to keep them safe at home.
who: Elderly or disabled adults who cannot protect themselves. Anyone can make a report, locally or through the statewide hotline at 1-800-458-7214.

name: Family Assistance (TANF)
summary: Temporary cash help for basic needs, paid on an EBT card, plus the JOBS program to help parents find and keep work.
who: Low income families with children under 18, or 19 if the child is a full time high school or vocational student. Apply at the Cullman County DHR office.

name: Child Support Services
summary: DHR can help find a parent, set up paternity, get a child support order and collect payments. The Cullman County office handles local cases.
who: Parents or caregivers raising a child who need child support set up, changed or enforced.
how: For the state child support office, call (334) 242-9300.

name: ALL Kids and Medicaid for Children
summary: Low cost or free health coverage for kids. Call to apply or to get an application mailed to you.

name: Brooks' Place Child Advocacy Center
summary: Supports children who may have been abused, and their families, with caring help.

name: Help Paying for Child Care (Child Care Subsidy)
summary: DHR helps pay for child care so parents can work or go to school. For Cullman County, the Child Care Management Agency (CMA) of North Central Alabama decides who qualifies and can refer you to child care providers.
who: Alabama families with low or moderate income who are working, in school or in training.

name: Find a Licensed Child Care Provider
summary: Search Alabama DHR's list of licensed child care centers and homes by county or city.
who: Any family looking for child care.

name: First Class Pre-K
summary: Alabama's nationally recognized pre-K program from the Alabama Department of Early Childhood Education, offered in local schools and centers.
who: Children who are 4 years old. Check the website for registration dates for the next school year.

name: Head Start and Early Head Start (CAPNA)
summary: Community Action Partnership of North Alabama runs Head Start in Cullman County, with early learning plus vision, health and dental screenings at no cost to families.
who: Children from birth to age 5 whose families meet program guidelines. Services vary by county, so ask what is offered near you.

name: Cullman City Head Start
summary: A Head Start program run by Cullman City Schools at Cullman City Primary School.
who: Eligible children and families who live inside the Cullman city limits.

name: Help Me Grow Alabama
summary: Free care coordination for families of young children. Share a worry about your child's growth, learning or behavior and a coordinator will help connect you to the right services.
who: Families with young children anywhere in Alabama.

name: Alabama Partnership for Children
summary: A statewide nonprofit focused on young children and families. It runs Help Me Grow Alabama and supports early learning programs.
who: Families with young children and child care providers.

name: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library
summary: Free books mailed to your child every month from birth to age 5. In Cullman County the program is run by the United Way of Cullman County.
who: Children 5 and under who live in Cullman County, no matter the family's income.

name: Women's Health and Family Planning
summary: The Cullman County Health Department offers women's health visits, Pap tests and family planning, with fees based on income.

name: The Willow Path
summary: Formerly Victim Services of Cullman, this group offers a 24 hour crisis line and emergency shelter for people facing abuse.

name: Cullman County Veterans Service Office
summary: Free help for veterans and families applying for VA benefits. Located in the Cullman County Courthouse.

name: Veterans Crisis Line
summary: Veterans in crisis can dial 988 and press 1, or text 838255. It's free, private and open 24 hours a day.

name: USA.gov Benefit Finder
summary: Answer a few questions to see government benefits you may qualify for, like food, health care, housing and help with utilities, and how to apply.
who: Anyone in the United States.

name: Social Security Administration
summary: Retirement, disability, SSI, survivor benefits and Social Security cards. Many services are online, and you can call to make, change or cancel an appointment.
who: Workers, retirees, people with disabilities and families.
hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. local time.

name: Medicare
summary: The official Medicare help line and website for questions about coverage, plans and claims.
who: People 65 and older and some younger people with disabilities.
hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, except some federal holidays.

name: LIHEAP Energy Help (CAPNA)
summary: The federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program helps pay heating and cooling bills. In Cullman County it is run by Community Action Partnership of North Alabama, by in person appointment only. Do not wait until your power is cut off.
who: Income eligible households in Cullman County. Bring all required documents to your appointment.
how: Book an appointment online or call the automated appointment line at (256) 260-4050.

name: 211 Connects Alabama
summary: Dial 211 any time, day or night, to talk with a trained specialist who can find food, housing, utility help, health care, jobs and senior care near you. It is free and private.
who: Everyone in Alabama.
how: You can also text your ZIP code to 898-211.
